text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London saw a last minute rally on Friday on the back of fund buying in New York. The benchmark August position finished the day $2.00 higher at $309.10 a tonne after having seen a peak of $312.50. The nearby August October spread widened with the rolling of spot positions into August, but traders said the spread was likely to slide down in the coming days.

Raw sugar futures in New York ended broadly higher, fueled by heavy fund buying in the nearby months, traders said. Interests focused on the nearby May/July switch at the outset, as speculators squared books ahead of the weekend. Commodity funds raced to buy the market once July cleared the widely-watched 11.00 cent barrier, driving prices to a one week high. The spot May contract rallied 0.33 cent, to 11.29 cents/lb while benchmark July futures 0.21 cent to close at 11.09 cents.

Traders said talk that Russia was an interested buyer also lent the market impetus, though no deals were confirmed. Friday's breach of 11.00 cents was seen as technically constructive, though the 11.18 mark would remain a tough hurdle, traders said. Support was noted at 11.00 cents, followed by 10.87 and 10.77-10.78.

FRANCE - Weather conditions for beet drillings were generally favourable in 1997 after a cold winter with little rain, the French Association of Beet Growers (CGB) reported. By April 15, sowings were completed which is around the same date as last year but around 10 days earlier than the ten-year average. Cold nights and the lack of precipitation slowed down the germination and the early development of the beet and the overall situation on April 15 was reported to be fairly heterogenous. In contrast to 1996 no damage due to rodents or frosts were reported. According to the CGB, the areas sown to beet (for sugar and alcohol) will be around the previous year's level.

NETHERLANDS - Sugar exports in December 1996 amounted to 32,469 tonnes, raw value, up from 29,744 tonnes in December 1995. This brought cumulative exports in the first quarter of 1996/97 (October/December) up to 79,309 tonnes, down from 111,127 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 301,918 tonnes against 381,586 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in October/December 1996 were Algeria with 30,476 tonnes whites against nil and Iran with 19,700 tonnes compared to 33,764 tonnes. Sugar imports in October/December 1996 reached 17,444 tonnes, hardly changed from last year's 17,827 tonnes. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 59,657 tonnes compared to 64,568 tonnes in 1994/95. The major country of origin in October/December 1996 was France with 8,149 tonnes whites compared to 8,664 tonnes.

BRAZIL - According to industry sources, Brazilian exporters expect to ship between 5.5 and 6.5 mn tonnes, tel quel, in 1997/98 (May/April). This compares with estimates of 5.3 mn tonnes in 1996/97, it was added.
However, this positive outlook depended on a number of factors:

(1) the level of prices on the world market and here a white sugar price in London of above $315 per tonne was seen as favourable for exports from the Center/South region while a price range of 10.80 to 11.20 cents/lb in New York could boost shipments from the North/Northeast.
(2) The price level for alcohol after the liberalization of the domestic market for anhydrous fuel starting on May 1, 1997.

The 1997/98 campaign in Brazil will start in May in the Center/South growing region. Initial expectations are that the cane crop will be up by 5 to 7 per cent on the previous year due to favourable climatic conditions and a higher area planted to cane. Despite the fact that growers recorded a lack of rainfall in the growing areas of Sao Paulo state and Parana in recent weeks, the cane is still in very good condition due to the high level of rainfalls in the preceding months. High temperatures during the day and low temperatures during the night have a positive impact on the maturing cane, it was added.
